research_goal: Create backend-ready MMA wrestling, clinch, cage-control, ground-control, submission, escape, and transition knowledge for SFTC. This draft focuses on what MMA athletes need beyond pure wrestling or pure grappling: strike-to-wrestle entries, wall wrestling, positional control, ground-and-pound, submission safety, and returning to the feet.

technical_principles.summary: MMA wrestling must connect strikes, clinch entries, cage pressure, takedowns, control, ground strikes, and stand-ups. Pure wrestling shots without strike setup or cage awareness expose the athlete to counters, sprawls, front headlocks, and fatigue.

Clinch control is built from head position, underhooks/overhooks, wrist control, hip position, posture, and foot placement. These determine whether the athlete can strike, turn, trip, defend, or separate.

Against the cage, athletes need pummeling, level-change timing, mat returns, wall walking, wrist fighting, hip heisting, and turning off the fence. The wall can support defense or help the attacker trap posture.

Beginners should learn position, base, posture, and safe escape before chasing submissions or strikes. Ground-and-pound and submissions are useful only when position and partner safety are controlled.

Scrambles should train decision trees: build base, win inside position, face opponent, control wrists, recover guard, stand up, or advance position. Random explosive effort wastes energy and can increase injury risk.

priorities: basic level change and penetration step without impact
positional hierarchy: guard, half guard, side control, mount, back
avoid_until_ready: heel hooks and twisting leg locks

priorities: single-leg and double-leg options with cage finish
takedown defense chains: sprawl, underhook, whizzer, circle, wall walk
positional sparring from cage, half guard, mount, back, and turtle
submission threat recognition and safe escapes
avoid_until_ready: hard wrestling on poor readiness days
stacking hard sparring, hard grappling, and heavy lifting

priorities: top control by score state and round time
camp-specific live rounds with load tracking
avoid_until_ready: high-risk submissions when joints are irritated
unplanned volume spikes in live wrestling or hard grappling

drills_or_practice_design: single-leg finish to cage mat return
half-guard top control to safe posture
mount escape technical bridge and elbow-knee path
ground-and-pound posture drill with soft targets
submission recognition and early tap drill
common_errors: shooting from too far without strike setup
dropping the head outside safe alignment on shots
accepting bottom position against the cage without building base
using ground-and-pound before posture and partner safety are controlled
turning away during scrambles and giving back exposure
doing live wrestling volume before neck, shoulder, hip, and knee tolerance is ready
safety_constraints: No uncontrolled high-amplitude throws for beginners.
No neck cranks, heel hooks, or twisting leg locks for beginners.
Stop or regress when neck, shoulder, elbow, wrist, knee, rib, or back pain worsens.
Ground-and-pound drills must use controlled targets, clear rules, and no head impact for beginner learning.
Do not pair hard live wrestling with heavy lower-body strength, hard sparring, or poor readiness.

sport_training_rules.rule: MMA wrestling should connect striking entries, clinch/cage control, takedown finish, positional control, and safe exit or attack.
recommended_action: Pair takedown entries with a strike or feint cue.
Teach the finish and next control position together.
Include escape and stand-up options for bottom athletes.
blocked_action: Do not prescribe isolated high-fatigue shots as the main wrestling method for beginners.
Do not use live takedowns before safe falling and control rules are learned.

sport_training_rules.rule: Cage wrestling should teach head position, underhooks, wrist control, hip pressure, foot position, mat returns, and wall-walk defense.
recommended_action: Use short pummeling and wall-walk rounds before live cage wrestling.
Teach attacker and defender responsibilities in the same block.
blocked_action: Do not run hard cage rounds when neck, shoulder, rib, or knee symptoms are increasing.

sport_training_rules.rule: Ground work should prioritize position, posture, base, frames, and escape pathways before submissions or ground-and-pound intensity.
recommended_action: Teach positional hierarchy and escape routes.
Use positional sparring constraints before open grappling.
blocked_action: Do not prescribe aggressive submissions or hard ground-and-pound before positional control and tap culture are reliable.

planning_rules.rule: Hard live wrestling, hard grappling, and hard sparring should not be stacked with heavy lower-body or neck/trunk loading on the same poor-readiness day.
recommended_action: Separate hard contact/grappling and heavy S&C by at least one recovery buffer when possible.
Use technical drilling or aerobic work when readiness is poor.
blocked_action: Hard live wrestling plus hard sparring plus heavy lower-body strength in one session for non-advanced users.

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build wrestling stance, motion, level change, sprawl, and safe takedown awareness without uncontrolled impact.
progression_signals: keeps posture and balance on level change
sprawls without neck or low-back symptoms
can safely reset after partner contact

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Link clinch position, cage pressure, mat-return attempts, and wall-walk defense under controlled partner resistance.
progression_signals: uses wall walk under controlled pressure
maintains breathing and posture through cage rounds

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Understand positional hierarchy, frames, base, posture, safe tap culture, and basic escapes before submissions or ground-and-pound intensity.
progression_signals: uses tap and verbal safety correctly

skill_assessments.summary: Assess MMA wrestling through stance, level change, shot setup, sprawl, underhook control, cage wall-walk, mat-return defense, and symptom response.
hold_if: neck, rib, shoulder, knee, or back symptoms worsen
athlete cannot fall, reset, or tap safely
panic or uncontrolled intensity appears during partner work

skill_assessments.summary: Assess ground skill through positional awareness, base/posture, escape quality, submission safety, ground-and-pound control, and fatigue response.
hold_if: hard head contact occurs in learning rounds
joint pain or neck symptoms worsen

minimum_evidence: 8+ completed MMA grappling or wrestling skill sessions
safe fall, sprawl, wall-walk, technical stand-up, and tap culture are reliable
no worsening neck, shoulder, rib, knee, or back symptoms
promote_when: can perform controlled partner entries and escapes
maintains posture and breathing under light resistance
uses safe reset rather than panic scrambling
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock controlled positional sparring and cage-wrestling drills, not hard live grappling.
